The Randolph Project is not projected to increase nor sizably decrease in number from the present community population of 12,000. No adverse affects are expected from the implementation of the renewal plan.
On the contrary the Randolph Communities statement of Goals and Objectives provides for the creation of adequate sites for a community center and other public facilities. Other physical and social goals are aimed at "after school training programs", "assistance for commercial enterprises", "provisions for recreational areas" and "establishment of educational and employment programs". The community proposes that the existing Randolph School building should become a Community Center, a physical center, in which the many goals and objectives of the community can take form. In addition to the building, the Randolph Plan provides for the creation of needed recreational open space and facilities in conjunction with the existing Randolph swimming pool. The Community Center will be located within the highest population area of Randolph which is also the area most remote from existing park and recreational facilities.
b. Health Facilities:
(1) There are no public or private health clinics or private doctors offices located in the Randolph Community. One pharmacy is located in the Randolph Community at the corner of Meadow Street and Idle-wood Avenue. The Virginia Home (for the Incurables), the only other health related facility in Randolph, is a specialized health service funded by the United Givers, located within the Randolph Community serving individuals from throughout the state. There are three hospitals in close proximity to the project area. Johnston Willis Hospital and The Retreat Hospital are located within one mile of Randolph and MCV Hospital is 1-1/2 miles away.
